notes.short: Two lines, two ways: the righteous and the wicked
notes.about: The second line answers the first with its opposite. Both lines speak of a way: the LORD guards one, and the other perishes.

lines.words: For the LORD guards the path of the righteous,
but the way of the wicked will perish.

original.note: In Hebrew both lines use the same word, derekh, “way”; the BSB says “path”, then “way”.

notes.evidence: Delitzsch (Keil and Delitzsch) sets the way of the ungodly against the way of the righteous. Barnes calls verses 4 to 6 a strong contrast between the unrighteous and the righteous. Henry: the Lord approves the way of the righteous and is angry at the way of the wicked, which shall perish.

cites.quote: God knows this way, which on this very account also unfailingly reaches its goal. On the contrary, the way of the ungodly … perishes, because left to itself

cites.quote: The Lord approves and is well pleased with the way of the righteous, and therefore, under the influence of his gracious smiles, it shall prosper and end well; but he is angry at the way of the wicked, all they do is offensive to him, and therefore it shall perish, and they in it.
